pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, repeat-dose study with 52-week primary analysis period (PAP) followed by open-label extension
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary: % change in % predicted DLco from baseline to Week 52; % change in spleen volume (MN) combined with change in splenomegaly-related score (SRS) from baseline to Week 52
pivotal_trials.result: DLco: LSM % change +24.2% (olipudase alfa) vs +3.08% (placebo), LSM difference 21.05% (95% CI: 13.65, 28.44), p<0.0001; Spleen volume: % change -38.8% vs +0.4%, LSM difference -39.22% (95% CI: -44.73, -33.70), p<0.0001; SRS component not significant (p=0.1533), combination endpoint failed per multiplicity strategy; trial deemed success on DLco endpoint

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, open-label, single-arm, ascending dose study in pediatric patients; 64-week treatment period
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: Safety and tolerability; Exploratory efficacy: spleen volume, liver volume, % predicted DLco
pivotal_trials.result: In mITT-C population (n=8, Process C only): mean % change in spleen volume -46.7% at Week 52; mean % change in liver volume -37.3% at Week 52; mean % change in % predicted DLco +50.6% at Week 52 (n=3 with DLco measurements); no control arm

boxed_warning.full_text:
WARNING: HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTIONS INCLUDING ANAPHYLAXIS

Patients treated with XENPOZYME have experienced life-threatening hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis. Appropriate medical monitoring and support measures, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation equipment, should be readily available during XENPOZYME administration. If a severe hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis) occurs, discontinue XENPOZYME immediately and initiate appropriate medical treatment. In patients with severe hypersensitivity reactions, a desensitization procedure to XENPOZYME may be considered.

key_safety: In pooled adult subjects (N=30), treatment-related hypersensitivity AEs occurred in 33% and infusion-associated reactions in 50%; in pediatric subjects (N=8), hypersensitivity AEs occurred in 50% and IARs in 75%, including one severe anaphylactic reaction in a 1.5-year-old; SAEs were reported in 33.3% of adults and 50% of pediatric subjects, with no deaths or permanent discontinuations due to AEs.
target_moa: Recombinant human acid sphingomyelinase (ASM) that provides exogenous ASM to hydrolyze accumulated sphingomyelin to ceramide and phosphocholine in lysosomes of affected tissues (liver, spleen, lung); does not cross the blood-brain barrier

_meta.indication: XENPOZYME is indicated for treatment of non–central nervous system manifestations of acid sphingomyelinase deficiency (ASMD) in adult and pediatric patients.

indication_details.population_restrictions: adult and pediatric patients; non–central nervous system manifestations only
